why: Both render the sentence before the break and Benedicta sis ... in aspectu tuo after it completely and correctly.
The fee list continues correctly on both sides (Camerario pro Chirothecis 1 fl.); the catchword Ca- is correctly dropped by both.

left_defects.source: Wer Abel / Seth / Enoch und Noah? Wer waren die Erzvaeter?
left_defects.translation: Were Abel, Seth, Enoch, and Noah, who were the patriarchs?

why: Left merges the two questions before the break into one garbled question; both handle keine | Doctores waren correctly.
Both close the petition list and open Sit queso sancte pater ... faithfully.
Both render so man zu ihm | ihm kommt once and translate the following sentences correctly.
In the sentence crossing the break, right takes the OCR Herz (Herr) literally as heart and renders the particle hin as down; left has neither error.

right_defects.source: Primus de pe. in cle. c. si qs
right_defects.translation: The first in Clementinae, c. si quis

why: Right drops the de poenis title in the citation just after the break; left punctuates The thirteenth. as a separate sentence, which breaks the flow but loses no content.

right_defects.translation: the 82-year-old man, deprived of his censorship

why: Right invents a meaning for depontanus (an aged man) in the sentence before the break; left renders it simply as the old man.

left_defects.source: facere profecto quod vice hac doleret
left_defects.translation: I would certainly regret having done this

right_defects.source: diligendis nulla de me ratio habita fuerit
right_defects.translation: in loving them, there was no gratitude toward me

right_defects.source: facere profecto quod vice hac doleret
right_defects.translation: I would certainly do what I would regret at this time

why: Right turns ratio into gratitude in the clause crossing the break and inserts an ellipsis there; both garble the at-si sentence.
Ceteri maxime | hoc factum admirantur and the following sentences are rendered correctly on both sides.
Left pulls the post-break verb back before the break, drops the novalia tithes, and drops the Secundus label; right keeps the structure and mistranslates only novalia.
Both render the last interrogatory and Reliqua interrogatoria ... correctly and drop the catchword.
Both carry locus | propitiationis across the break as one clause, with no losses.
Both close the Laudate sequence and open Cantate ... canticum nouum faithfully.

left_defects.source: Quid est quod ullo tempore apud te magno studio contenderim, nisi a te hoc etiam atque etiam exigo
left_defects.translation: What is it that I have contended for ...? I demand this from you again and again

why: Left breaks up the rhetorical question before the break and adds an ellipsis at admonui | ut; right keeps the construction intact.
Left translates the catchword An as well as the real An, which leaves a stray duplicated Whether at the break.
